page: Amazon Web Services c9g.48xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the arm64 architecture, this instance features 192 dedicated physical cores running at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz, with a single thread per core. It is equipped with 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

The c9g.48xlarge does not include local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent data. It provides a baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps. A key architectural consideration is the arm64 instruction set, which requires compatible software builds. Additionally, the compute-focused design allocates a lower memory-to-core ratio compared to general-purpose or memory-optimized instances, which may limit memory-bound workloads.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the custom Graviton arm64 architecture is designed to deliver high compute density and energy efficiency compared to traditional x86 architectures. This makes the instance suitable for highly parallelized, compute-intensive workloads that scale across many cores, such as batch processing, video encoding, and distributed analytics, provided they do not require local storage or high memory-per-core ratios.
